A capital P sits inside a rounded square over a quarter-divided circle. The composition may be a presentation brand mark or a pie-chart badge; text and geometry have three distinct reusable parts.

## Visual draft

A large circle is divided by two radii into a visible upper right quarter. A rounded square badge overlaps its left side and contains a single upright capital P.

## Open question

Should the intended result preserve a specific presentation logo or depict a generic pie chart with a P badge? Reuse the existing P glyph in either case.

## 1. Quarter divided pie chart (solo)

A circle is divided by upward and rightward radii into a visible upper right quarter. Exclude the overlaid letter badge.

## 2. Rounded square letter badge (container)

An empty rounded square badge provides a plain enclosure for a single letter. Exclude the capital P and background pie chart.

## 3. Uppercase P typeface layout (typeface)

Reuse exact uppercase P with preferred glyph letter-p-uppercase and its existing paths in icon_set/typeface/glyphs.json, centered in the badge with natural proportions. Exclude invented letter geometry, the chart, and badge outline.

Either approach must follow the requested family's design rules and preserve the named subject's identity. Apply this only to the named component and exclude the other components. Keep the original reference unchanged.

Typeface components must follow the reuse instructions above, never new icon generation.
